question: Each third-grade classroom at Pearl Creek Elementary has \(18\) students and \(2\) pet rabbits. How many more students than rabbits are there in all \(4\) of the third-grade classrooms?
solution:
Each classroom has \(18-2=16\) more students than rabbits. There are four classrooms, each with this same difference, so altogether there are
\[
4(18-2)=4\cdot16=\boxed{64}
\]
more students than rabbits, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).

edges.reason: Mental addition prepares place-value decomposition and inverse checks. Borrowing and teen-subtraction facts compute a mental difference directly, so an entire mental-addition procedure is not necessary.
edges.scope: two-digit subtraction as inverse of addition

edges.reason: Borrowing in general two-digit subtraction includes teen-minus-two-through-five subtractions in the units stage.
The equal-addend sum being rewritten as a product contains chained addition. The subtraction half of the endpoint is not required.

Written addition prepares vertical alignment and repeated carrying. In multiplication the carried amount is added to one digit product, so the full three-digit column-addition procedure is not executed.

The general digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm contains digit products with seven, eight and nine. Their values are required, without demanding rote recitation as the exclusive way to obtain them.

Two-digit division broadens which expression steps can be computed. The precedence convention and a three-step calculation can also be practiced with one-digit divisors; the wider algorithm is preparation.
